screen: Title card: "Phophy: find anything in your photos, on your iPhone". Team 26
voice: This is Phophy, an iPhone app that understands your photo library, built by Team 26.

screen: Problem card: thousands of photos, receipts, slides, screenshots
voice: A phone holds thousands of photos. Finding the receipt from last week or the slide about TCP means minutes of scrolling, and sending everything to a cloud AI costs money and gives your photos away.

Phophy reads every photo once, on the phone: the text in it, what it shows, and an embedding. A small AI model writes a short description. Search combines all of that. Nothing leaves the phone unless you choose a cloud model.

screen: App: Library, scroll Recents, open a receipt, info sheet (where, description, text)
voice: Here's the library. Open a photo and Phophy shows what it knows: where it was taken, a description written on the phone, and every word on the receipt.
Search understands what you mean. A scene, a place, even a typo or a Chinese word. Each answer takes about 20 milliseconds.

screen: Search: "G1234", "receipt from Muji", "whiteboard with the network diagram"
voice: It also finds words written in photos, and photos described in a sentence, like the whiteboard from our group project.
Collections sorts the library for you: slides, receipts, documents, pets, screenshots. And it finds bursts of near-identical shots, suggesting which one to keep.

screen: Study: three lectures → open TCP lecture → Make notes → summary, key points, flashcards
voice: Students photograph lecture slides and never look at them again. Phophy groups them by lecture, and in a few seconds turns them into a summary, key points and flashcards, using only the text on the slides.

screen: Assistant: "How much did I spend at Muji?" → HK$702
voice: You can also just ask. The assistant searches your photos with tools and reads the answer from the receipt.

screen: Assistant: "When does my train to Shanghai leave?" → 08:15
voice: When does my train leave? It finds the booking screenshot and reads the time.

screen: Assistant: "Put my photos from the Tokyo trip in an album" → Save album
voice: And it can organise: here it gathers the Tokyo trip into an album, which you confirm with one tap.

screen: Editor: open a beach photo, type "warmer and brighter", Done
voice: Edits work the same way: describe the change, and it runs on the phone for free.

screen: Settings: who describes photos, the cloud warning alert
voice: Everything runs on the phone by default, with Apple Intelligence or a small open model for older iPhones. If you choose a cloud model, Phophy warns you first that your photos leave the device.

screen: Results card: search before and after
voice: We measured search on a standard benchmark, Flickr30k. Compared with our first version, Chinese searches went from 2% to 51% correct in the top ten, misspelled searches from 13% to 59%, and objects found in the top 50 from 51% to 89%, while long descriptions stayed as accurate as before.

screen: Results card: speed on an iPhone 13 Pro Max
voice: On a real iPhone 13 Pro Max, without Apple Intelligence, search takes under 25 milliseconds and the on-device model describes a photo in about one and a half seconds.

screen: Team card: four members and their parts
voice: Phophy was built by Su Chuanzhou, Yin Fengling, Qin Mengmeng and Wang Zhengyao. Thank you for watching.
